profile_text.body:
Arm is a public company founded in 1990 and headquartered in Cambridge, United Kingdom. On its own site, Arm describes itself as providing the compute platforms behind advanced AI, spanning cloud, edge, and physical AI, with consistent software and flexible compute across an ecosystem. It says its technology powers everything from cloud infrastructure and personal devices to AI-defined vehicles and robotics, and it points to an Arm AI Portal where developers and agents can discover optimized models, evaluate performance, and access deployment workflows. The site also references an AGI CPU, discussed by Arm's Eddie Ramirez, and NVIDIA's Open Agent Safety Platform as an example of Arm powering agentic AI, along with NVIDIA DGX Spark built on Arm-based NVIDIA Grace Blackwell technology.

The held facts record no products tracked for Arm and no lawsuits. The only other entries associated with the company are a set of MCP servers listed under its record, covering data observability tools, a hosted Google Calendar server, a contractor search service, career frameworks, a Karma library, Korean drug ingredient lookup, an ad board, a pharma vendor-services server, and a night-fishing game. None of these descriptions identify Arm itself as the provider.
